cards.title: Raising a Child With Ultra-Rare Genetic Disorder
cards.body: A parent shares their journey raising a daughter with a one-in-163-million genetic condition. After decades in film PR, they're now fighting their biggest campaign yet: their child's survival and wellbeing.

cards.title: Teaching Kids Essential Life Skills Like Cooking
cards.body: Middle-class parents often neglect teaching practical skills like laundry and food preparation. Young people need these competencies before leaving home for university.

cards.title: Parenting Through Difficult Moments With Grace
cards.body: When a child gets sick in the car, stress can overwhelm even the most prepared parent. Small acts of kindness from strangers can provide crucial support during these challenging situations.

cards.title: Preparing for University: The IKEA Parenting Test
cards.body: The pre-university shopping trip to IKEA reveals how much domestic wisdom parents have actually taught their children. It's a wake-up call for many about gaps in practical parenting.

cards.title: Discovering Suburban Family Life's Hidden Joys
cards.body: Moving to the suburbs seemed boring until a family discovered excitement in unexpected places. Sometimes parenting in quieter communities offers unexpected benefits.

cards.title: Parenting a Child With Schizophrenia: Real Advice
cards.body: A father shares his experiences and offers guidance for parents caring for children with schizophrenia. Understanding this mental health condition helps families navigate the unique challenges it presents.

cards.title: Five Cognitive Frames to Teach Your Children
cards.body: Certain lessons parents teach kids only make sense as they experience the world. Passing down these mental frameworks helps children develop resilience and wisdom.

cards.title: Understanding Gifted Children's Burnout and Boredom
cards.body: High-IQ and gifted children often suffer burnout from too much work volume, not challenge. Parents should focus on providing meaningful, substantive activities rather than simply keeping them busy.
